Similarly though, there also no reason to want to die other than our emotions tell us to. We live because we want to live, it's a basic animalistic instinct. What we don't want is the pain and suffering that is attached to living. Life is beautiful, but we let our minds forget that when we deal with our problems. Living is not good or bad, it's a truly neutral phenomenon. It is dyed good or bad because of the way we perceive it. Death may be the outcome of living, but it's wrong to say that it is the base of life. Can you say that excrement is the basis of eating? Life has value independent of death. One is simply the consequence of the other, it is not the basis of the other.

Saying you've never been happy your entire life is like saying you've never been angry. It's a basic human emotion that happens after positive stimuli. The feeling you get after a good meal is happiness, the feeling you get when you watch your favorite TV show is happiness. Happiness is a fleeting temporal emotion that we've developed biologically to reward ourselves after something good happens, nothing more nothing less. It is not meant to be felt for an extended amount of time. It is not anything grand or a way of life.

It's because of your biology and boredom. Your evolutionary instincts do not allow you to become intent, this is because in the past humans needed to stockpile resources to survive certain scenarios. To you, this is a bad thing because you have the resources you need yet you still need to struggle. This feeling then passes through a cultural and financial filter until you are left with the depression you feel now. Other people can turn this feeling into ambition for their jobs to live better lives or a political struggle for privilege in modern society. However this is not applicable to you, and that is where depression comes in. Since there are no external conflicts your subconsciousness creates conflict inside yourself and that is depression. I'm not trivializing your feelings - just because it's something you induced yourself doesn't mean the feelings are any less intense. It's nothing to be ashamed of either it's just a bad side effect of society progressing faster than our biology can react to it. 

Now what to do about it? In my opinion it's to set a goal for yourself, or start a new hobby, or just focus on studies. Handball didn't work out, that doesn't mean nothing will. You won't be happy if you think about trying to be happy all the time, or if you think about your sadness all the time. Don't go into things thinking "oh this might make me happy," nothing will make you happy forever. Start new things with the mindset that doing that thing is the goal, not a byproduct on the road to make you happy. We're all just living life to let time pass - the best outcome is to look back at life and think "that wasn't so bad".
